mcqs.question: A gas in a piston is heated while the piston is locked, and then the gas expands against a movable piston without any temperature change. Which statement correctly distinguishes the heat transferred in the first process from the work done in the second process?

options.A: In the first process, energy is transferred as heat because the temperature of the gas rises; in the second process, energy is transferred as work because the gas does boundary work on the piston.
options.B: Both processes involve only heat transfer.
options.C: Both processes involve only work transfer.
options.D: Heat and work are the same form of energy transfer.

mcqs.answer: In the first process, energy is transferred as heat because the temperature of the gas rises; in the second process, energy is transferred as work because the gas does boundary work on the piston.
mcqs.explanation: Heat is energy transferred due to a temperature difference, occurring when the piston is locked. Work is energy transferred when a force moves a boundary, which happens during the expansion against a movable piston. Options B, C, and D confuse the two distinct modes of energy transfer.

mcqs.question: A gas expands from 2 L to 5 L against a constant external pressure of 1 atm. According to the physics sign convention, what is the sign of the work done by the system?
mcqs.explanation: In physics, work done by the system on the surroundings is taken as negative because energy leaves the system. Since the gas expands, it does work on the surroundings, so the work is negative. Positive work would correspond to work done on the system, which is not the case here.

mcqs.learning_point: Calculate work in simple thermodynamic processes
mcqs.question: A gas in a cylinder is compressed from 10 L to 4 L at a constant external pressure of 2 atm. What is the work done on the gas? (1 L·atm = 101.3 J)
mcqs.explanation: ΔV = 4 L – 10 L = –6 L. Work done by the system = PΔV = 2 atm × (–6 L) = –12 L·atm = –1215.6 J. Work done on the gas is the negative of this, +1215.6 J. The common mistake is to assume work is always negative; here the system is being compressed, so work is done on it.

mcqs.question: In a PV diagram, a process from point A (P = 2 atm, V = 3 L) to point B (P = 2 atm, V = 8 L) is shown as a horizontal line. Which statement correctly describes the work done by the gas during this process?

options.A: Zero work because the pressure is constant.
options.B: Positive work because the volume increases at constant pressure.
options.C: Negative work because the pressure is constant.
options.D: Work cannot be determined without temperature information.

mcqs.answer: Positive work because the volume increases at constant pressure.
mcqs.explanation: Work = ∫P dV. With constant pressure, W = PΔV = 2 atm × (8 L – 3 L) = 10 L·atm, which is positive (energy transferred from system to surroundings). Option A is wrong because constant pressure does not imply zero work; only constant volume does. Option C misinterprets the sign, and D is unnecessary.

mcqs.question: Consider two processes involving 1 mol of an ideal gas at 300 K. Process I: The gas is heated at constant volume, absorbing 500 J of heat. Process II: The gas expands isothermally against a constant external pressure, doing 500 J of work on the surroundings. Which statement correctly compares the two processes?

options.A: Both processes increase the internal energy of the gas by the same amount.
options.B: In Process I, the energy transfer is solely as heat, whereas in Process II, it is solely as work.
options.C: Process I results in a temperature rise, while Process II also results in a temperature rise.
options.D: Both processes have the same sign for energy transfer according to the physics sign convention.

mcqs.answer: In Process I, the energy transfer is solely as heat, whereas in Process II, it is solely as work.
mcqs.explanation: At constant volume (Process I) no boundary work is possible, so the 500 J enters the system only as heat. In an isothermal expansion (Process II) the internal energy of an ideal gas does not change, so the 500 J leaves the system solely as work. Option A is false because internal energy changes differ; C is false because the isothermal process keeps temperature constant; D is false because the signs are opposite (heat added vs. work done by the system).

mcqs.question: A gas expands from 1.0 L to 3.0 L while absorbing 250 J of heat from the surroundings. If the work done by the gas on the surroundings is 150 J, what is the change in internal energy of the gas? (Use the physics sign convention where work done by the system is negative.)
mcqs.explanation: First‑law: ΔU = Q + W_on_system. Q = +250 J (heat added). Work done by the gas = +150 J, so work on the system = –150 J. ΔU = 250 J + (–150 J) = +100 J. The positive sign indicates the internal energy increases. Options B, C, and D arise from sign errors.

mcqs.learning_point: Calculate work in simple thermodynamic processes
mcqs.question: A piston‑cylinder contains gas at 1 atm pressure. The gas expands reversibly from 0.5 L to 1.5 L at constant pressure. What is the magnitude of work done by the gas? (1 L·atm = 101.3 J)
mcqs.explanation: Work = PΔV = 1 atm × (1.5 L – 0.5 L) = 1 L·atm = 101.3 J. The other options correspond to incorrect multiples of the pressure‑volume change.

mcqs.question: On a PV diagram, a vertical line segment represents which of the following processes?
mcqs.explanation: A vertical line means volume does not change while pressure varies, which is the definition of an isochoric process. An isobaric process would be horizontal, isothermal curves are generally hyperbolic, and adiabatic processes have a distinct curved shape.
